summary: Move the CLC before ADC col_ptr into the rare v_ptr page-crossing path: the common path reaches save_on_page through BCC taken, so C is already 0 there.
equivalence: save_on_page has one entry besides fall-through: the BCC at 1529 (grep: no other reference; the label is local to draw_column's scope). Taken path: C=0 by the branch condition; TXA, TAY, EOR #&FF change only N and Z, so C=0 at ADC col_ptr exactly as after the old CLC. Not-taken path: C=1 (ADC #11 carried), INC v_ptr+1 leaves C, the moved CLC makes C=0 before TXA/TAY/EOR, so ADC col_ptr again sees C=0. A, X, Y, memory and every flag after ADC are identical on both paths (CLC only ever changed C, which ADC then overwrites; N/Z/V are set by ADC). BCC's offset grows from 2 to 3, far within range. Cost: 2 cycles saved on each of the 13.1 hot executions a pass (CLC measured 26.2 cycles), plus 2 cycles added on the 0.46 page-crossing executions (INC measured 2.3 cycles at 5): net 25.3 cycles a pass; same byte count. No paging, self-modified operand or data involved; the interrupt saves and restores P.
relies_on: save_on_page is reached only by fall-through from INC v_ptr+1 and by the BCC at line 1529; TXA/TAY/EOR # do not alter C (65SC12).

.last_cell
    DEC A                           \ 65C02 opcode
    STA stop_y
.part_byte
    LDA (v_ptr),Y
    STA (s_ptr),Y
    DEY
    CPY stop_y

new:
.last_cell                          \ rows_m1 = Y - the last line: rows_m1 + 1 bytes to put back
    LDX rows_m1                     \ (X is free in columns: .more reloads it)
.part_byte
    LDA (v_ptr),Y
    STA (s_ptr),Y
    DEY
    DEX
    BPL part_byte
summary: The last cell's byte loop counts X down from rows_m1 with DEX/BPL instead of storing Y-rows_m1-1 to stop_y and comparing with CPY stop_y: 2 cycles less on entry, 1 less per byte, 2 bytes smaller.
equivalence: last_cell is reached only from cell's BCS (Y >= rows_m1, A = Y - rows_m1, rows_m1 <= Y <= 7). Old: stop_y = Y - rows_m1 - 1, the loop copies lines Y down to Y - rows_m1: rows_m1 + 1 bytes, exits with Y = Y0 - rows_m1 - 1. New: X = rows_m1 (0..7) and DEX/BPL runs rows_m1 + 1 times, the same bytes in the same order, same exit Y. On exit A, flags and X differ (X = $FF, was the record's low byte): JMP columns reloads A and flags at once; X is reloaded by TAX at .more before any use, and at columns' RTS X is dead (the part 3/2 caller PLXes it back, part 1's continues to blocks_done, which LDXes back); Y at the RTS is dead too (LDY rb_index after both JSRs). stop_y is no longer written here; its only other user, draw_column, stores it before its loop. rows_m1 is only read. Entry: DEC A + STA zp 5 -> LDX zp 3; per byte CPY zp 3 -> DEX 2. 13.13 entries + 47.53 bytes a pass (measured line cycles / per-execution) = ~73.8 cycles; 7 -> 5 bytes.
relies_on: X dead in restore_block's columns walk from last_cell to .more/RTS (PHX/PLX around the part 2/3 call, LDX back after part 1); rows_m1 <= 7 at last_cell so BPL counts it; stop_y not read after restore_block (draw_column sets it first).

At the BCS, C set iff Y >= rows_m1 (unsigned), Y is X AND 7 or 7, so rows_m1 <= Y <= 7 and BPL counts X = rows_m1 down through 0: rows_m1 + 1 bytes, same lines in the same order as old (stop_y = Y0-rows_m1-1, $FF when equal), same exit Y. Exit JMP columns sets A and flags at once; v_ptr/s_ptr untouched. X: .more's TAX reloads it; at columns' RTS the part 3/2 call is wrapped in PHX/PLX (1838-1840) and part 1's is followed by LDY rb_index / JMP blocks_done / LDX back, so restore_block still exits with X = back; Y reloaded by LDY rb_index on both returns. stop_y (&C6) no longer written here: only draw_column reads it in the renderer, after its own STA (1591 before 1603); compiled restore code never names &C6; &C6 is not in save/restore_game_zp (zplive: logic's first access after a render is never a read; frames/y/mover_x_max_high/result_high are written first in the routines read), and draw_column already leaves arbitrary values there. irq1_handler does not use &C6 or rows_m1; registers saved by the interrupt. summary: JMP columns after the last cell becomes BRA columns: 1 byte smaller, same 3 cycles while columns (&9E72) and the branch (~&9EE5) share a page; independent of the other two.
equivalence: Unconditional either way, same target, no flags or registers touched. Offset from &9EE7 to &9E72 is -117, in range (less if the other candidates shrink the code between). A 65C02 taken branch costs 3 cycles, plus 1 only if it crosses a page: both addresses are in page &9E in the current listing.
relies_on: columns and the instruction after the BRA staying in the same page (now &9E72 and &9EE7); if code before them moves so that they straddle a page, this costs 1 cycle an execution and should be dropped.

skeptics.reason: The only way in is falling through from BNE part_byte (Z=1). The JMP has no label, and no source or tool refers to its address by label+N, a table or a self-modifying store. The only way out is to columns, which reads only memory (v_ptr, rb_end) and sets A and the flags itself, so neither BRA nor JMP touches anything that is live. Neither one changes registers, flags or the stack. An interrupt sees the same state either way. Listing: the JMP is at &9EE5, so BRA ends at &9EE7, giving offset &9E72-&9EE7 = -117, which is in range. The target and the next instruction are in page &9E, so the taken BRA costs 3 cycles, the same as JMP abs. Saves 1 byte, 0 cycles, as long as columns and the instruction after the BRA stay in the same page.

Machine lens holds. BRA (&80) is a 65SC12 opcode (the file already uses BRA; DATA1 is cmos = TRUE). Listing: JMP columns at &9EE5 (4C 72 9E), columns at &9E72. New BRA at &9EE5-&9EE6, next PC &9EE7, offset &9E72-&9EE7 = -117 (&8B), in range; same page &9E, so taken BRA = 3 cycles = JMP abs 3: 0 cycles an execution, 1 byte saved. Neither touches flags or registers. No SMC targets this instruction or any label near it; nothing reads this code as data (generators read sprites, no literal addresses into &9EE8-&B39A anywhere in src). The one-byte shift of everything after (&9EE8 to the end of bank 4's code and tables, no ALIGN): no branch changes page-crossing state (scanned all branches in and into the region, including BMI compiled at &9E8E); no label or abs,X/Y table target in the region sits at a page start, so every abs-indexed read there crosses no more often than before (low bytes drop by 1 without wrapping). Caveat for the gate, not a refutation: (zp),Y walks through the straight sprites in bank 4 at run-time offsets may reshuffle page crossings by the shift (net zero in expectation, either sign per sprite), and the moved renderer variables (rb_part2, list_*, arena_top_*) are the project lens's call under 'no data moves'.

Only write_column writes src0-7+2, and the calls do pair up: each push is the last call of one render and the first of the next. So 9.5 a call holds. The +5-byte shift of everything after &9654 in bank 4 is what refutes it. I built both versions in scratch and diffed the listings. (1) compact's per-byte copy loop: BNE counted moves from &9FF7 to &9FFC and now jumps to &A002, across a page, so every taken branch costs +1, about 3.7 cycles a pass from the measured 11.1. Only BEQ listed and BCS none stop crossing. Measured with passbench, seed 1, passes 500-2500, A=HEAD vs B=candidate, both built in scratch. Mean render is 24176 in both, so the 6.9 a pass never shows. Logic went 13351->13354. The worst passes got 2-7 cycles slower (1651: 120238->120240, 1653: 113598->113603, 1675: 105405->105412). Passes over 2 fields went 93->95, and fields went {1:47,2:1885,3:68}->{1:49,2:1881,3:70}: two more 3-field passes. As one change it is not faster and is slightly slower at the worst. It would need padding or an ALIGN so the compact loop, need and list_y1 keep their pages.

Project lens: not refuted. The candidate touches no PROTECTED line, no generated source and no data or table: write_column is hand-written renderer code in src/render.6502 (bank 4). The only memory it guards is its own 8 self-modified operand high bytes (src0..src7 + 2, &966D..&9697). A grep over src/ finds no other reader or writer, and nothing copies or reloads this code in place: bank 5 gets the &9300 tune unpack, not bank 4. All 8 assemble equal (ASSERT HI(hist0-8)=HI(hist0-1), hist_src_hi holds only HI(hist0-1)/HI(hist1-1)), and they are only ever written together, so src0+2 = A implies all 8 = A. Paging: the code runs from bank 4 at &96xx with ROMSEL &84 or &04. ANDY covers only &8000-&8FFF, and ACCCON's X bit affects only &3000-&7FFF, so CMP abs reads the same bank-4 byte the STAs write. Registers and flags: A is dead after it, and LDX #&C8 sets N/Z. The C that CMP sets is dead: the loop sets it with SEC/CLC before every use. V is untouched. Room: bank 4 has &B39A-&B400 = 102 bytes free; +5 leaves 97, and the ASSERTs still hold. hist0/hist1 are fixed at REN_BASE+&400/&500 and do not move. Nothing in DATA1 is ALIGNed, and outside code takes bank-4 addresses from the shared symbol table. The BEQ (&9652->&966C) and the loop's own branches stay within page &96. Behaviour is the same on every path (front end, helicopter, game over, completion, define controls): the skip happens only when the stores would rewrite identical bytes. Cycles: equal 7 against 32 (saves 25), unequal 38 (costs 6). Each push's slot is applied once to each screen, the two screens consume the same alternating slot sequence (hist_next EOR #1), and every render applies its pending entries oldest first. So about half the calls match the one before: 9.5 a call, as claimed (reasoned, not measured; the gate's passbench measures it). Possible second-order cost: the rest of bank 4 shifts by 5 bytes, which could make some other branch or table read cross a page. That is timing only, and the gate catches it. bytes_recounted is -5 in the claim's convention: the code grows by 5 bytes (CMP abs 3 + BEQ 2).

Stack: JSR/RTS balanced, the two bytes below S are dead; depth at exit unchanged. Interrupts see nothing different beyond timing. Cycles: 12 saved, confirmed. Bytes: the claim of -3 is miscounted: inline is 6 bytes replacing a 3-byte JSR (+3 if width_of_type_A is kept); width_of_type_A (7 bytes) becomes dead and deleting it gives -4. The applier should delete the routine and record -4.

Machine lens: AND #imm, TAX, LDA abs,X are base 6502 opcodes, so they are valid on the 65SC12. width_of_type_A (&9775) has one caller (render.6502:429, &92C2). No code stores into it and nothing reads it as data (grep of src/ and tools/). mover_types_width_table is at &16D7 in main RAM below &3000, so ROMSEL and ACCCON paging do not affect the read, and it is the same absolute operand (BD D7 16) as inside the subroutine. X = type AND &7F, but the table only has entries 0..&1B, so the read is at most &16F2 and no page is crossed in either version. Flags at span_in_zone are N/Z from the LDA in both versions (RTS changes no flags), and span_in_zone starts with CLC. Cycles: old JSR 6 + AND 2 + TAX 2 + LDA abs,X 4 + RTS 6 = 20, new 8, so 12 saved per execution. Bytes: the call site grows from 3 to 6, i.e. -3 under the positive-is-smaller convention, which matches the claim. If the now-dead 7-byte subroutine is deleted too, the total is +4 smaller. Side effect, not a refutation: shifting the rest of bank 4's renderer by +3 changes the page crossing of a few later taken branches by 1 cycle each (BEQ taken_off &92FD, BEQ listed &97FD, BCS none &9CFD, BNE counted &9FF7). This is noise for the measured speed gate.

Not refuted. The inlined AND #&7F / TAX / LDA mover_types_width_table,X are width_of_type_A's body (render.6502:837-841), run from the same bank-4 code at the same point, so the paging state (ROMSEL, ANDY, ACCCON) is the same. The candidate's 'relies on' is wrong in one detail: the table is in game.6502 at &16D7 (main RAM), not in render.6502. That does not matter, because &16D7 is below &3000: ACCCON's X bit cannot send the read to shadow RAM, and ANDY (&8000-&8FFF) does not cover it. Results: A = width, X = type AND &7F, Y kept, N/Z from the LDA, C untouched in both versions. span_in_zone clears C, reads A and reloads X from zone_n, so nothing after the call sees a difference. The stack is two bytes shallower for the moment the call would have lasted, which nothing can observe. No protected, generated, data, zero-page or raster-timed code is touched. width_of_type_A has no other caller (grep of src and tools), but the diff leaves it in, so the region grows by 3 bytes: 6 inline against the 3-byte JSR. That matches the claim's bytes of -3 (positive = smaller). Bank 4 ends at &B39A against REN_BASE &B400 (102 free), so it fits. Everything that moves after it is referenced by label, and the page-alignment ASSERTs are on hist0 (REN_BASE + &400) and column_buffer (&0300), which are fixed. Cycles saved: JSR 6 + RTS 6 = 12 an execution. Deleting the dead subroutine as well would save 7 bytes, a net 4 smaller.

.clip_test                          \ j = n - c unflipped, c - 1 flipped (c = columns left)

.have_j

new:

    LDA ds_n
    SEC
    SBC ds_c
    BRA have_j                      \ 65C02 opcode

    BIT dm_flip
    BPL unflipped_j
    LDA ds_c
    DEC A                           \ 65C02 opcode
.have_j
    CMP dm_jmin
    BCC to_next                     \ left of the viewport
    CMP dm_jmax
    BCC visible                     \ not right of it: j < jmax...
    BEQ visible                     \ ...or j = jmax

summary: Clip test: the jmax test becomes CMP dm_jmax; BCC visible; BEQ visible on j, which is already in A, so ds_j is no longer stored and reloaded. The flipped path falls through, the unflipped block moves into the dead space after .to_next's JMP next, and LDA ds_c runs only on the flipped path. Does not overlap the other candidate.
equivalence: The only entry is BMI clip_test (line 1492). .unflipped_j sits after the unconditional JMP next, so nothing falls into it. have_j keeps its name (tools/colfast.py matches draw_column.have_j). BIT dm_flip sets N from dm_flip bit 7 as before (BIT overwrote the old LDA ds_c's flags) and V from bit 6 as before. Unflipped, A = ds_n - ds_c (the same SEC;SBC); flipped, A = ds_c - 1 (the same). That is identical for every value, jmax=&FF included. X (the lowest line) and Y (8) are untouched on both paths. At visible, A, C, Z and N differ (A=j, not jmax; C may be 0). visible starts with LDA b_ptr (sets A, N, Z), and C is next read only after SEC (up_cell) or CLC (raised: LDA v_ptr; CLC). At next (j > jmax), C is now 1 where it was 0. next is DEC ds_c; BEQ done; BIT, then CLC/SEC before any ADC/SBC. done is the RTS out of ren_draw_sprite. Its callers (lines 1330, 1351, 1361) do CMP #2, CLC, or RTS out of draw_mover, and draw_mover's only caller (line 1189) does LDA v_ptr; CLC before reading C. ds_j is no longer written: its only reader was the removed CMP ds_j (grep of src and tools), and the byte stays where it is. Exits: at visible A, N, Z, C differ; visible does LDA b_ptr then TXA (N,Z), up_cell does SEC before SBC, raised does LDA v_ptr; CLC before ADC: C and A dead, V unchanged anyway. At next (j > jmax) C is 1 not 0, A = j not jmax: next does DEC ds_c; BEQ done; then BIT dm_flip and CLC/SEC before any ADC/SBC; done is RTS to ren_draw_sprite's callers: after 1330 LDX/LDA/CMP #2 (C rewritten); after 1351 LDX/LDA/BNE nothing -> RTS from draw_mover, and after 1361 -> RTS from draw_mover; draw_mover's only caller (1189) does LDX/LDY/LDA v_ptr/CLC before reading C. BCC to_next
    INC col_ptr + 1
.to_next
    JMP next
new:
BCS empty_hi                    \ the page crossed (rare)
.to_next
    JMP next
.empty_hi
    INC col_ptr + 1
    BRA to_next                     \ 65C02 opcode
summary: Empty column: the common path, where no page is crossed, falls through BCS (2 cycles) into JMP next instead of taking BCC (3 cycles) to it. The page-cross INC moves out of line. Saves 1 cycle an empty column; 2 bytes larger. Does not overlap candidate 1: both apply, and candidate 1's .unflipped_j then follows BRA to_next.
equivalence: Reached only by falling from STA col_ptr after LDA col_ptr; CLC; ADC #2 (the empty path). .to_next stays the target of BCC to_next in have_j, with the same meaning (JMP next). No carry: falls to JMP next exactly as the taken BCC did. Carry: INC col_ptr+1, then BRA to_next -> JMP next, as before. A, X, Y and C are identical on reaching next: C=1 on the carry path in both versions, 0 otherwise, and INC/BRA/JMP leave C alone. Z/N differ only on the carry path, and next starts with DEC ds_c. empty_hi is a new label, unique in the draw_column scope.
relies_on: Measured: STA col_ptr runs 4.17 times a pass and BCC is always taken (the profile never executes the INC), so the rare path's +4 cycles do not count. Bank 4 has 2 bytes to spare under the render ASSERT (below &B600).

skeptics.reason: Semantics hold on every path. Entries: .empty only from BEQ empty in .each (line 1474); line 1443 is BRA each so nothing falls into .empty; .to_next is referenced only by BCC to_next in have_j (line 1465) and the new BRA (no other users in src/, no tables, no label+N). Exit is always JMP next, no stack use. No-carry path: old BCC taken -> JMP next, new BCS not taken -> JMP next: A, X, Y, memory, C=0, V and N/Z (from ADC) identical. Carry path: same single INC col_ptr+1 write; N/Z from the INC in both (BRA/JMP touch no flags), C=1 and V from ADC in both, so every flag is identical. Nothing an interrupt could see differs: same stores in the same order. Self-modified operands move +2 but are written only by label. Built the candidate in a scratch copy (RELEASE=1, -Shift 256 -ShiftEnd with/without DEBUG_FULLREDRAW, DEBUG_LIVES+FULLREDRAW): all assemble. Recount from the listing: BCS &9BC5 not taken 2 + JMP 3 = 5 vs BCC taken same page 3 + JMP 3 = 6: 1 saved; carry path 14 vs 10 (+4). Bytes +2 (saved -2). Caveat for the gate, not a refutation: the 2 bytes shift everything after draw_column.empty in bank 4 by +2 (render workspace, sprite_column_count, ck_* tables, straight_sprite_lo/hi, straight sprite data). Behaviour is unchanged (all by label), but page crossings change: BCS none at &9CFF no longer crosses when taken (-1), LDA straight_sprite_lo,X now crosses for X=&49,&4A (+1), LDX ck_index,Y for Y=&2F,&30 (+1), and (col_ptr)/(d_ptr),Y crossings in sprite data shift. Machine lens holds. All opcodes real on the 65SC12 (BCS, INC zp, BRA = 65C02 in a cmos = TRUE section; no Rockwell bit ops). Recount at the current listing (.empty &9BBE): old BCC to_next at &9BC5 is taken to &9BC9 on the same page = 3 cycles, new BCS empty_hi not taken = 2, so 1 cycle saved an execution with no page-crossing case on either side; the carry path goes from 2+5 = 7 to 3+5+3 = 11 (+4). Not counted by the claim: the +2 bytes move everything after it in bank 4 (need, list_y1, ck_index, straight_sprite_lo sit near page ends; the straight sprite data; BCS none at compiled_part stops crossing a page), so the real change differs from 4.17 a pass. Faster on both games, so not refuted, but the claim's 4.17 is not the measured figure.

.up_cell
    TAX
    LDA s_ptr
    SEC
    SBC #&80
    STA s_ptr
    LDA s_ptr + 1
    SBC #&02
    CMP #&40
    BCS up_in_ring
    ADC #&40
.up_in_ring
    STA s_ptr + 1
    TXA
    CLC
    ADC #8
    BCC up_cell
.raised                             \ A = the line of the lowest byte drawn
    TAX

new:
.up_cell                            \ X = the line, negative: a cell up for each 8
    LDA s_ptr
    SEC
    SBC #&80
    STA s_ptr
    LDA s_ptr + 1
    SBC #&02                        \ C stays 1: the high byte is &40 or more
    ORA #&40                        \ round the 16K: &3D-&3F to &7D-&7F, &40-&7F unchanged
    STA s_ptr + 1
    TXA
    ADC #7                          \ C = 1: + 8
    TAX
    BCC up_cell
.raised                             \ A = X = the line of the lowest byte drawn
    ORA s_ptr                       \ the record's address
summary: Drop the TAX at .raised (A = X already on the hot BPL path; the cell-up loop does its TAX at the bottom instead of the top), and in that loop replace CMP/BCS/ADC #&40 with ORA #&40 and use the known C = 1 after SBC #&02 for ADC #7 in place of CLC; ADC #8. Overlaps the second candidate (its alternative).
equivalence: Hot path (TXA; BPL raised, ~11.3 a pass): A = X already from the TXA, so the TAX at .raised is redundant. Loop path: the TAX at the top of up_cell moves to after the ADC, so each iteration still updates X (on entry X = the line: from the TAX at 1482, or via clip_test -> BCS visible, which never touches X), and on the fall-through out of the loop A = X, as the removed TAX at .raised gave. TAX does not touch C, so BCC tests the ADC's carry as before. In the loop, SBC #&02 on a high byte of &40-&7F (minus at most 3 with the low byte's borrow) never borrows, so C = 1 after it; ORA leaves C alone, so TXA; ADC #7 gives the same A and carry as TXA; CLC; ADC #8. ORA #&40 equals CMP #&40/BCS/ADC #&40 (C=0 on that path) for every A in &00-&7F (A < &40: bit 6 clear, so A + &40 = A OR &40; &40-&7F: unchanged by both). After .raised: A = X = the line and Y = 8 as before; C is not live (next C use is the CLC at 1526); N/Z come from the ORA as before; s_ptr/s_ptr+1 hold the same values. No other references to up_cell, up_in_ring or raised anywhere in src/ (up_in_ring is removed). Same RAM, same paging, no new RAM.
relies_on: s_ptr+1 (copied from b_ptr+1) is in the screen ring &40-&7F on entry to up_cell, as everywhere in the renderer (raise_address, the flipped adjust, step_back/forward and compiled_part's unsafe restore all keep b_ptr+1 in &40-&7F; movers' screen addresses are in &40-&7F). Cycles: 2 on each of the 13.1 executions of .raised a pass (26.2) plus 5 an iteration of the loop (CLC 2; CMP+BCS taken 5 -> ORA 2) on ~1.9 iterations a pass (9.5).

skeptics.reason: Entries: only fall-through from TXA/BPL raised at 1498 (A = X = the line; X from the TAX at 1482, untouched on the clip_test -> BCS visible path) and the loop's own BCC; no other references to up_cell/up_in_ring/raised in src or tools; no self-modification or tables point into the range. Loop: X now updated by TAX after ADC instead of at the top, so X = A at every BCC and at the fall-through into .raised, as the removed TAX there gave. C after SBC #&02 is 1 whenever s_ptr+1 >= 3; ORA keeps C, so ADC #7 with C=1 gives the same 9-bit sum, so the same A, C, N, Z and V as CLC; ADC #8. ORA #&40 equals CMP #&40/BCS/ADC #&40 for every result in &00-&7F and &C0-&FF; they differ only if s_ptr+1 is in &00-&02 or &82-&C2 on entry, which cannot happen: s_ptr+1 = b_ptr+1, from raise_address (which keeps dm_scr_hi, a mover screen address, in &40-&7F and wraps it), the flipped adjust, step_back/forward (wrap to &7F/&40) and compiled_part's unsafe restore of the same b_ptr; the loop itself keeps it in &40-&7F, and old code at such a value would already write outside the screen. After .raised: A = X = the line, ORA gives the same N/Z, C dead until the CLC at 1526, V identical anyway; s_ptr/s_ptr+1 receive the same values in the same order, so an interrupt sees nothing different; no stack use. Cycles: 2 a .raised execution; loop iteration old 9 (10 wrapping) vs new 4, so 5 (6) more an iteration. Bytes: 9 old vs 3 new: 6.

Not refuted. Every opcode is plain NMOS/65SC12 (LDA/STA zp, SEC, SBC/ORA/ADC #imm, TXA/TAX, BCC, BPL); no page crossings in the changed lines (zp and immediate only). Listing: BPL raised at &9C1D, up_cell &9C1F; new raised = &9C34 and BCC at &9C32 -> &9C1F, all page &9C, so no branch takes a page-cross cycle; ranges tiny. Bytes: old up_cell..TAX at raised = 27 (&9C1F-&9C39), new 21: 6 saved. Cycles: hot path (TXA; BPL raised taken) loses the TAX at raised: 2. Loop iteration: old 31 (no wrap) / 32 (wrap) + BCC, new 26 + BCC: 5 / 6 a pass round the loop, the TAX moved not removed, the exit's TAX gone (counted in the 2). Semantics on the machine: C = 1 after SBC #&02 needs s_ptr+1 >= 3 on each iteration; b_ptr+1 comes from raise_address (in-cell path passes movers_screen_address_high through; the game builds those with its wrapping add/subtract helpers and the original plots there, so &40-&7F), the flipped adjust (BPL/-&40), step_forward (BPL else &40), step_back (<&40 -> &7F) and compiled_part's unsafe restore, all &40-&7F; ORA #&40 then keeps s_ptr+1 in &40-&7F, so inductively C = 1 and ORA #&40 = the old CMP/BCS/ADC #&40 (they differ only for A in &80-&BF, i.e. a high byte &82-&C2, never reached). TXA; ADC #7 with C=1 gives the same A and carry as CLC; ADC #8 (no SED anywhere in src/). Exit A = X = the line as before; C dead (CLC at 1526); V not live. No self-modified operands in the lines; mask_operand/pix_operand etc. after it are referenced by label and the writers at 1298-1320 follow them. Caveat for the gate, not a refutation: the 6 bytes come out of DATA1 ahead of everything up to SKIP PAD_END, so sprite_column_count, ck_*, straight_sprite_lo/hi, bank 4's straight sprites and the render variables all move down 6. Recounted: LDA straight_sprite_hi,X (&A501 -> &A4FB) then crosses a page for every sprite >= 5: +1 on each of ~4.55 executions a pass (up to +4.55); straight_sprite_lo stops crossing at X=&4B, ck_index (&A3CF -> &A3C9) stops crossing for Y &31-&36, list_y1 (&A2EC -> &A2E6) crosses for X >= &1A instead of >= &14 (all savings); and (d_ptr),Y/(col_ptr),Y crossings in bank 4's straight sprites (&A54D on) shift by 6, data-dependent either way. So the 35.7 a pass is the window's figure; the net is likely ~30 but only the gate's measurement settles it. No branch in bank 4 changes its page-crossing status (all 184 checked against the listing shifted by 6).

Checked in src/render.6502. Entry to up_cell is only the fall-through of TXA/BPL raised (1498-1499), where X = A = the line from TAX at 1482 (clip_test -> BCS visible touches A, flags, ds_j only, never X), and the loop's BCC up_cell, where the new TAX after ADC keeps X = A; so dropping the TAX at the top is exact. summary: close_over_overlaps .gather: drop the CLC, since C=0 from CPY act_n not-equal (Y counts up from 0 by one and stops at act_n, so Y < act_n here); STY/LDX/STX/TXA leave C alone.

Y is 0 on the first pass (LDY #0) and ren_k+1 thereafter (from .not_listed, which every path reaches), ren_k being the previous Y; act_n is not written in close_over_overlaps or anything it calls (list_live, list_recorded, list_finish, widen_by_live, world_of_address - grep: act_n written only at render.6502 393/440, before mark_to_draw), and ren_k only by the STY here. So Y increases by 1 from 0 and stops at act_n (<= MOVER_SLOTS), hence Y < act_n when not equal and CPY leaves C=0. STY abs, LDX abs,Y, STX abs, TXA do not affect C, so ADC boff sees C=0 exactly as after CLC. Every later state identical.
relies_on: act_n constant during close_over_overlaps and Y never exceeding it; ren_k not written by the subroutines called from the loop.

skeptics.reason: The only entry to .gather's body is the fall-through of CPY act_n / BEQ gathered (.gather is local to close_over_overlaps' scope, reached only from LDY #0 and BRA gather after .not_listed; every path through the body, shown/listed/not_listed, reaches LDY ren_k / INY). Y starts at 0 and steps by 1; act_n is written only by STZ/INC in step 1 (render.6502 393, 440) before mark_to_draw/close_over_overlaps, and no callee (list_live, list_recorded, list_finish, widen_by_live, world_of_address) writes act_n or ren_k (their stores go to list_*, wa_* only; list_slot etc. lie after act_n/ren_k and are indexed <= MOVER_SLOTS within their MOVER_SLOTS+1 size). So at the body Y < act_n unsigned and CPY leaves C=0; STY abs, LDX abs,Y, STX abs, TXA leave C alone, so ADC boff sees C=0 as after CLC. No exit or flag state differs (CLC changed only C, which was already 0). An interrupt saves and restores P, so it cannot change C between CPY and ADC. Stack untouched. Saves CLC: 2 cycles, 1 byte per execution.

Whenever BEQ gathered falls through, Y < act_n, and CPY act_n leaves C=0. ren_k (EQUB at 2259) and act_n (2265) are written by name only in render.6502, and not inside list_live, list_recorded, list_finish, widen_by_live or world_of_address. Every opcode is plain NMOS/65SC12. Removing CLC saves 2 cycles and 1 byte on every execution, with no page-crossing or branch-taken path involved. The only branch across the removed byte, BRA gather (backward), gets shorter and stays in range. No self-modifying operand or code read as data in this window. Bank 4 code after this point moves down a byte; the build's ASSERTs and the timing gate catch any branch that crosses a page differently afterwards.

Hence Y climbs by 1 from 0 and BEQ exits at Y = act_n, so on fall-through Y < act_n unsigned and CPY leaves C=0; STY/LDX abs,Y/STX/TXA leave C alone (an IRQ restores P on RTI), so ADC boff sees C=0 as after CLC. Not a PROTECTED line, not generated or data, not raster-timed; runs in bank 4 with the same RAM touched; it only shrinks the code by a byte (the hist ASSERTs and render_end ASSERT would catch any layout break at build time). Only entry to the changed lines is fall-through from TAY in close_over_overlaps (labels shown/not_listed/listed are local to its scope; the classify loop's own 'shown' at 404/418 is a different scope; close_over_overlaps is only JSRed from 449). No path reads A, N or C produced by the changed instruction. INC A is used elsewhere in the source with Baron, so it assembles. CMP #imm 2 bytes/2 cycles, INC A 1 byte/2 cycles: 0 cycles, 1 byte saved.

INC A (&1A) is a real 65C02/65SC12 opcode, 1 byte, 2 cycles, already used throughout render.6502 (lines 414, 639) so Baron accepts it in this cmos section; CMP #&FF is 2 bytes, 2 cycles. No self-modifying operand here (rec_xh is fixed workspace at REN_BASE+&180, nothing stores into this code), no code-as-data. Shrinking bank 4 code by one byte moves later code/tables but render_end <= REN_BASE ASSERT only gains slack; any page-crossing change downstream is for the gate's measurement, not this window. 0 cycles, 1 byte.

equivalence: Line 2157 is STA wa_off+1 and line 2158 TAX, so X = wa_off+1. Lines 2159 LDY wa_rows_guess,X, 2160 LDA wa_off and 2161 CMP wa_rows_base_lo+1,Y change neither X nor wa_off+1, and there is no label in between (the only entry is .world_of_address). TXA gives A the same value as LDA wa_off+1 and, like it, sets only N and Z, leaving C from the CMP for the SBC. The SBC at 2163 then overwrites N and Z. skeptics.reason: Checked in src/render.6502. The only entry into world_of_address is its label (JSR at lines 995 and 2135). Nothing else references it, row_known or wa_off: grep finds only these lines and the workspace at line 2282. Inside the routine there are no labels before row_known and no self-modifying stores. Line 2157 STA wa_off+1, then 2158 TAX, so X = wa_off+1 (0..63). Neither LDY wa_rows_guess,X nor LDA wa_off nor CMP abs,Y writes X or wa_off+1. TXA puts the same value in A that LDA wa_off+1 would, and like LDA it sets only N and Z. It leaves C from the CMP for the SBC, and V and D are untouched by both. The SBC then rewrites A, N, Z, C and V, so nothing that differs survives. X, Y and memory are the same at every exit, and so is the stack, since neither instruction touches it. The memory byte wa_off+1 is still stored and is read again after row_known. An interrupt between the TAX and the TXA saves and restores X, and the interrupt code never mentions wa_off. If it did write that byte, the old code would be the one that changed, not the new. The saving is TXA 2 cycles and 1 byte against LDA abs 4 cycles and 3 bytes: 2 cycles and 2 bytes. The machine and project skeptics should check that shrinking bank 4 by 2 bytes does not move a later table across a page boundary and change an indexed read's cycles.

Checked src/render.6502 2149-2166. The TAX at 2158 follows STA wa_off+1, so X = wa_off+1. LDY abs,X (2159), LDA abs (2160) and CMP abs,Y (2161) leave X and wa_off+1 alone. The only entry is .world_of_address (called from 995 and 2135), and row_known comes after. Nothing in src/ stores into this code: there are no label+1/+2 writes and no '= * + 1' labels here, and the bytes are not read as data. wa_off is an EQUB at line 2282 in bank 4 (&9000+), so LDA wa_off+1 is LDA abs: 3 bytes, 4 cycles, no indexing and no page crossing. TXA is 1 byte, 2 cycles, a real 65SC12 opcode (&8A). It sets N and Z from the same value and leaves C from the CMP for the SBC at 2163, which overwrites N, Z, V and C anyway. The SBC abs,Y page-crossing cost is the same in both versions. BCC row_known still jumps over the 1-byte INY, so the range is fine. Saves 2 cycles and 2 bytes on every path.

Checked src/render.6502 2149-2198: world_of_address has one entry (callers at 995 and 2135, both JSR to the label), no label between the TAX at 2158 and the LDA at 2162, and LDY abs,X / LDA abs / CMP abs,Y leave X alone, so X = wa_off+1 (0..63) at 2162. TXA sets N,Z only, keeping C from the CMP for the SBC, and the SBC rewrites N,Z,V. wa_off+1 is still stored and read at 2171; X on exit is unchanged (still wa_off+1), so callers see the same registers. Not PROTECTED, not generated, not raster-timed; reads no different RAM under any ROMSEL/ACCCON state (wa_off is bank-4 workspace, TXA touches no memory). Shrinking render.6502 by 2 bytes fits its region; the hist/rec workspace is at fixed REN_BASE offsets so its ASSERTs are unaffected; later render labels shift by 2 as any code shrink does (page-cross cost of indexed tables is for the gate's measurement). LDA abs 4 cycles/3 bytes vs TXA 2 cycles/1 byte.

Alternative to candidate 2 (overlaps).
equivalence: Entries are the two routine labels only (JSR from callers). Add, old: delta_low=dl[Y], delta_high=dh[Y], A=lo+dl (CLC), Y=that, A=hi+dh+C, wrap if N, X=high result, A=Y=low result, N/Z from TYA, C/V from the high ADC (or SEC/SBC #&40). New: delta_high=hi (temp), X=dl[Y], delta_low=dl[Y], CLC, A=lo+delta_low (same sum and C), X=dh[Y] (LDX keeps C), Y=low result (TAY keeps C), A=dh, ADC delta_high = dh+hi+C: addition commutes, so A, C, V, N, Z equal the old hi+dh+C; STX delta_high=dh[Y] touches no flag, so BPL tests the same N; tail unchanged. Subtract, old: A=lo-dl (SEC), Y=that, A=hi-dh-borrow, CMP #&40/BCS/ADC #&40, TAX, TYA. New: delta_high=hi (temp), delta_low=dl[Y] via X, SEC, A=lo-delta_low (same result and C), X=dh[Y], Y=low result, A=delta_high=hi (LDA keeps C), delta_high=dh[Y] (STX keeps flags), SBC delta_high = hi-dh-borrow: same A, C, V, N, Z; the CMP tail and exits unchanged. Both exits: A=Y=low byte, X=high byte, N/Z of the low byte, C/V as before, delta_low/delta_high as before (rows_up's documented leftovers &79/&02 hold), D untouched. Cycles per execution: add 16 x 3.03 (18.2/6), subtract 15 x 2.35 (14.1/6). Bytes: add part 10 -> 19, subtract part 10 -> 20, helper's 13 removed: +6 (so bytes = -6).
relies_on: No interrupt reads &B6/&B7 (irq1_handler and sfx_tick in play, the MOS's IRQ on the front end), so delta_high may hold the address's high byte for the few instructions before its final store; get_screen_address_delta has no callers outside these two routines (grep src/: lines 2076 and 2100 only; tools/frontend.mjs names it only in a trail-filter regex); nothing reads the stack bytes below SP that the old JSR/PHA wrote; the deltas tables (&1D94, &1D9D, Y 0..8) sit before the code so do not move; the code after &1DA6 moves, which the gate's speed and split checks cover (the protected irq1_handler span from &2D9D has no branch that crosses a page after an 8-byte shift); bytes fit the 31 free before &3400 (compiled_back &33E0)

Add path: new A after first ADC = lo+dl[Y] with the same C; LDX/TAY/TXA keep C; second ADC computes dh+hi+C against old hi+dh+C - same A, C, N, Z and V (V is symmetric in the operands); STX delta_high touches no flag so BPL sees the same N; tail unchanged; exit A=Y=low, X=high, delta_low=dl[Y], delta_high=dh[Y]. Subtract path: A=hi via LDA delta_high (C kept), then SBC delta_high(=dh[Y]) is the same hi-dh-borrow with the same operand order, so A, C, V, N, Z equal; CMP/BCS/ADC tail unchanged; rows_up's leftovers (&79/&02, C, V) hold. D is never set (no SED in src/). Interrupt: irq1_handler (and sfx_tick, bank 5 variables at &A5xx, sfx_request &2E57) never reads or writes &B6/&B7 or any alias (first_mover, target, edge_and_layer, frame_and_flip, last_mover), so the transient delta_high=hi is invisible; IRQ preserves X/Y/A. Stack: old pushed a return address and A below SP and popped them; new pushes nothing; depth at every exit equal and nothing reads below SP. Table reads identical (&1D94/&1D9D + Y 0..8, no page cross). Cycles: add 45->29 (16 saved), subtract 45->30 (15 saved); weighted by 3.03 and 2.35 executions a pass = 83.7 cycles a pass, 15.56 an execution. Bytes: add +9, subtract +10, helper -13: code grows 6 (bytes saved -6).

Machine lens, checked against the source and the bench listing (build/strykers-shift256end-debug_lives.lst). Opcodes: STX zp, LDX abs,Y, STX zp, CLC/SEC, ADC/SBC zp, TAY, TXA and LDA zp are all NMOS opcodes, so they are valid on the 65SC12; none of BBR/BBS/RMB/SMB is used. Flags: LDX, TAY, LDA and STX leave C alone, so the low byte's carry or borrow reaches the high ADC/SBC. In binary mode ADC is commutative, so A, C, V, N and Z are the same for dh+hi+C as for hi+dh+C (D is clear in play, and old and new both use ADC anyway). SBC keeps its operand order (A=hi, M=dh). The STX delta_high between the high ADC and the BPL changes no flag. Both exits leave A=Y=low byte, X=high byte and delta_low/delta_high=dl[Y]/dh[Y], the same as before. Cycles: the old helper is JSR 6 + PHA 3 + LDA abs,Y 4 + STA 3 + LDA abs,Y 4 + STA 3 + PLA 4 + RTS 6 = 33. The tables are at &1D94-&1DA5 (ship) and &1D98-&1DA9 (bench) and Y is 0..8, so neither table read crosses a page. Add: old 33+12=45, new 3+4+3+2+3+4+2+2+3+3=29, saving 16. Subtract: old 45, new 3+4+3+2+3+4+2+3+3+3=30, saving 15. Weighted: (16x3.03+15x2.35)/5.38=15.56. Bytes: add 10->19, subtract 10->20, helper's 13 removed: 33->39, so the code is 6 bytes larger and bytes saved is -6, as claimed. Branches: BPL skips 3 bytes and BCS skips 2, both in range. Self-modifying code: nothing writes into these routines or the deltas tables (grep for label+1/+2, skip_wraparound_*, leave_1d68). There are no raw numeric absolute addresses in &1D00-&33FF anywhere in src/. The page-sensitive ASSERTs (the green pixel and mask tables at &0440, sound_data_0880) are either at fixed addresses or before the change. The code after the change moves up 6 bytes. In irq1_handler's protected span, BEQ not_vsync_2ee3 (&2DAD bench, &2DA9 ship, both +6) and BNE to_leave_irq1_handler stay within page &2D. wait_for_vsync_2242's BEQ (&22D2 -> &22D8, target &22D6) stays within page &22. So the protected raster timing is unchanged. Interrupts: irq1_handler and sfx_tick do not touch &B6/&B7. The title IRQ handler runs only on the front end, where these routines are not called. On its own the change fits the 31 bytes free before &3400, and the build's ASSERT guards it.

Not refuted. I checked the semantics by hand. On the add path A = dh+hi+C, which gives the same A, C, V, N and Z as before because addition commutes. On the subtract path A = hi-dh-borrow, as before. delta_low and delta_high still end as dl[Y] and dh[Y], so rows_up's &79/&02 leftovers hold, and so does what the logic reads at &B6/&B7 after a render (&B7 is also frame_and_flip). The temporary &B7 = hi could only be seen by an interrupt. irq1_handler, sfx_tick and the title IRQ chain (update_scrolltext, plot_title_screen_character, multiply) never name &B6/&B7 or any of their aliases, and the MOS IRQ does not use &B0-&BF. Every caller is a JSR in game.6502; none is in render.6502 or the banks. The tables are below &3000 and Y 0..8 does not cross a page, so the RAM read is the same whatever ROMSEL or ACCCON's X bit hold. get_screen_address_delta has no other callers. The lines are not protected and not generated. Room: the code grows by 6 bytes (39 against 33), and 31 are free before &3400. Everything after &1DB2 moves +6, by label only: nothing in src/ names an address in that range as a number. The protected irq1_handler span becomes &2DA3-&2DF6, all in page &2D, with no indexed reads. wait_for_vsync_2242's loop stays within one page. The interrupt's variables stay below &3000 (ASSERTed). Shadow &3000-&3FFF is copied from main at render_reset, so the moved code and data there stay mirrored. Nothing from &3400 up changes. One side effect: irq1's BPL no_flip no longer crosses a page, so the code after the palette writes takes 1 cycle less. Cycles: add 45 -> 29 (16 saved), subtract 45 -> 30 (15 saved). Weighted: 83.7 a pass, 15.55 an execution. Bytes saved: -6.

The STX that follows leaves flags alone, so BPL still tests the sum's N. On subtract, LDA delta_high keeps C, so hi-dh-borrow is the same as before. The exit A, X, Y, C, V, N and Z, and the final delta_low/delta_high, are identical on both paths.     STA keys_pressed_bitmap
    LDY #&00
.check_for_player_input_loop
    LDA keys,Y
    EOR #&FF                        \ INKEY number -> internal key number (check_for_keypress, inlined)
    TAX
    INY
    STY key_to_check                \ keydown_int clobbers X and Y
    JSR keydown_int                 \ A = &80 if down, else 0
    ASL A                           \ C = down
    ROR keys_pressed_bitmap         \ key Y-1 in at bit 7: after eight, key N is bit N
    LDY key_to_check
    BCC check_for_player_input_loop \ C = 1 only when the sentinel falls out (Y = 8)
.leave_2f89
    RTS
summary: check_for_player_input: check_for_keypress inlined (JSR keydown_int direct). Each key's bit goes in by ASL A/ROR into a bitmap seeded with an &80 sentinel, and the sentinel falling out into carry ends the loop. No shift loop, no zeroing, no CPY. It costs a constant 262 cycles plus the RTS a call, whatever keys are down. Exit state is identical except A/Z/N, which are dead. Alternative to candidate 2 (they overlap).
equivalence: The only entry is check_for_player_input (JSR from main_game_loop, lines 2792 and 2796). check_for_player_input_loop, skip_shift, shift_loop and key_not_pressed have no other references. It reads the same eight keys, in the same order 0..7, with the same keyboard read. check_for_keypress is TXA/EOR #&FF/TAX/JSR keydown_int/EOR #&80; here it is inlined as LDA keys,Y/EOR #&FF/TAX/JSR keydown_int, so keydown_int sees the same X. keydown_int returns A=&80 if the key is down, else 0, so ASL A gives C=down. The original sets bit k of a zeroed bitmap for each pressed key k (EOR acts as ORA because each bit is set only once). The label stays at the PLA; leave_irq1_handler (with the self-modified JMP whose high byte is written as leave_irq1_handler + 7) is unchanged in content and layout relative to its own label.

So A,X,Y,P,PC,S and &FC are identical at the RTI exit, whatever path (including the title handler chaining in with its own &FC). I is set from IRQ entry to RTI: no CLI in irq1_handler; sfx_tick's code has none (sfx50's only PHP/SEI/PLP is sfx_silence, which keeps I set). A after PLA is the stacked copy of &FC, STA &FC leaves it there, PLY/PLX touch only Y, X, N, Z, so the reload gives A the same value. Its N/Z are then overwritten by the P that RTI pulls. Nothing can write &FC in between: I has been set since the IRQ was taken (sfx_tick's PHP/PLP put it back), and an NMI would not touch the MOS's IRQ byte. Both ways in (falling through from vsync, JMP leave_irq1_handler_owned from T1) arrive with the same stack. The changed code comes after the protected raster-timed code (irq1_handler..LDA top_palette_value and not_vsync_2ed0..STA ula_palette) and after wait_for_vsync_2242 (&22CA), so none of their timing moves. summary: Replace the second LDA flip_screen with AND #&01: A is (acccon AND &FE) OR flip_screen, and flip_screen is only ever 0 or 1.
equivalence: After STA acccon, A = (ACCCON AND &FE) OR flip_screen (the register value, not a re-read of ACCCON). AND #&01 gives bit 0 of that = flip_screen's bit 0 = flip_screen, since flip_screen is written only by render.6502:531 from `back` = shown_screen EOR 1, and shown_screen is only STZ'd or set from flip_screen, both starting at 0, so it is 0 or 1 by induction. STA shown_screen stores the same byte; Z/N differ only transiently (A=0/1 either way gives the same Z, N=0 both) and the next instruction STZ then BIT irq_owned sets N,Z,V anyway. No label between the lines; entry only by fall-through from STA acccon.
relies_on: flip_screen in {0,1} (render.6502 back = shown_screen EOR 1); A unchanged since ORA flip_screen (STA does not change A). Shrinks the handler by 1 byte (interrupt variables move down by 1, symbol-referenced; combined with the other two candidates 5 bytes).

skeptics.reason: Entry only by fall-through from STA acccon (no label between game.6502:4523 and .no_flip; nothing branches in). At that point A = (ACCCON AND &FE) OR flip_screen, untouched by STA, so AND #&01 = bit 0 of flip_screen. flip_screen's only writer is render.6502:531 (STA flip_screen from back); back's only writer is render.6502:323 (shown_screen EOR 1); shown_screen is written only by STZ (render.6502:228, 587) and this STA from flip_screen; all start 0 (EQUB 0). By induction flip_screen and shown_screen are always 0 or 1, so the stored byte is identical. Flags: both leave N=0, Z=(flip_screen==0), C/V/D untouched; STZ flip_pending changes none, then .no_flip's BIT irq_owned overwrites N,V,Z and the paths after it (PLA at leave_irq1_handler, or LDA #&02) kill A and test no flag before setting it, and C is not read before RTI restores P. The handler runs with I set, so no nested interrupt between the lines; the main-line readers (render, render_to_main) see the same shown_screen value. No stack change. Cycles: LDA abs 4 -> AND # 2, saves 2; bytes 3 -> 2, saves 1.

Holds on the 65SC12. Old: LDA flip_screen is absolute (&2E5D, not zero page): 4 cycles, 3 bytes, no indexing so no page-crossing term. New: AND #&01 immediate, 2 cycles, 2 bytes, a real 6502 opcode (&29). Saves 2 cycles and 1 byte on the flip path (once per flip), the other paths do not reach it. A at that point is (ACCCON AND &FE) OR flip_screen (STA acccon leaves A alone), so bit 0 is flip_screen's bit 0 and bits 1-7 come from ACCCON. AND #&01 equals flip_screen only if flip_screen is 0 or 1. Checked: flip_screen (EQUB 0) is written in src/ only at render.6502:531 from back (&A18A, bank 4 EQUB 0). back is written only at render.6502:323 as shown_screen EOR 1. shown_screen is written only by STZ (render.6502:228 and 587) and by this handler from flip_screen, so both stay 0 or 1 by induction. No indexed store reaches them: sfx_request,X uses X 0-3 only, and flip_pending, flip_target and irq_owned are never indexed. Flags: N=0 and Z the same either way, C and V are not touched, STA and STZ change no flags, and the BIT irq_owned at .no_flip sets N, V and Z again before any branch. There is no label between the two lines and no self-modifying operand here (previous_irq1_vector_low is later and found by its symbol). The 1-byte shift of the interrupt variables and the code after them up to the SKIP unused_3400_original is reached only through symbols (the tools use syms, ASSERT shown_screen < &3000 still holds, and the sprite tables use LO/HI of labels), and SKIP keeps everything from &3400 where it was.     ADC sfx_p_lo,X

new:
LDA sfx_dp,X                    \ the period steps (16 bits, the step sign-extended)
    BPL up
    DEY                             \ Y = 0 from sfx_write (sfx_output ends in it): &FF, the step's high byte
.up
    CLC
    ADC sfx_p_lo,X
    STA sfx_p_lo,X
    TYA                             \ the step's high byte, 0 or &FF
    ADC sfx_p_hi,X
    STA sfx_p_hi,X
summary: Period step: sign-extend the step into Y (Y=0 on return from sfx_output, DEY if negative) instead of reloading sfx_dp and branching to LDA #0 / LDA #&FF; TYA feeds the high-byte ADC.
equivalence: Old: positive step 33 cycles (LDA4 CLC2 ADC4 STA5 LDA4 BPL3 LDA#2 ADC4 STA5), negative 35; new: positive 29 (LDA4 BPL3 CLC2 ADC4 STA5 TYA2 ADC4 STA5), negative 30 (BPL2 DEY2): measured split ~1.55 positive / 0.25 negative a pass from BPL's and the LDA #0/#&FF lines' counts gives ~7.45 cycles a pass. Bytes 27 -> 20. The low add is the same (A = dp, C cleared, + p_lo, stored); DEY/TYA leave C alone, so the high add is A = 0 or &FF (sign of dp, as before) + p_hi + the same carry: same A, C, N, Z, V and same stores. The only entry is the fall-through from JSR sfx_output (labels up/add_high are local to sfx_tick's scope and referenced only here; add_high disappears). Y differs afterwards (0 or &FF instead of 0): the rest of the loop never reads Y (LDA sfx_dv... DEC sfx_n, BNE next; sfx_next_ramp does LDY #0 first; the next channel's request path sets Y by TAY, sfx_output's tone path reaches sfx_write's LDY #&FF before any Y read, its noise path never reads Y), and sfx_tick's only caller (game.6502 irq1 handler) PLYs the interrupted Y after it; the old exit Y was already path-dependent.
relies_on: Y = 0 on return from sfx_output: every path of sfx_output ends by falling into sfx_write, whose last loop (LDY #4 .. DEY BNE) leaves Y = 0 (the annotation shows Y=$00 at line 40). If sfx_write's tail ever changes, this must change.

Flags at the JSR differ (N/Z from LDA hi rather than LDA #&FF) but sfx_next_ramp sets them before use. Saves DEC A (2c,1B) and LDA #&FF (2c,2B).

summary: Drop the second LDA (scenery_sprite_address),Y in find_end_of_column_loop: A already holds that byte (BEQ does not change A), so AND #&C0 works on the same value.
equivalence: The first LDA (zp),Y loads the byte at the same address (Y and the pointer &CE/&CF unchanged in between); BEQ only reads Z and leaves A, X, Y, C, V. On the zero path nothing changes. On the non-zero path the removed reload put the identical value in A and set N/Z identically; AND #&C0 then overwrites N and Z from A exactly as before, so A, Z, N, C, V, X, Y and memory are the same at the BNE and on every later path (the loop, the INY/BNE variable-run path, move_to_next_column). No label is on the removed line, nothing branches to it or reads it as data or modifies it; the pointer is main-RAM data read with the same paging as the first LDA one instruction earlier, and an interrupt between the two loads cannot change scenery sprite data (sprite data in game RAM, not written by the IRQ). relies_on: The scenery sprite bytes at (&CE),Y are not changed by an interrupt between the two loads (they are static sprite data).

Between the two loads there is only BEQ, which reads Z and changes nothing, so Y and the pointer &CE/&CF are the same. On the BEQ-taken path the removed instruction never ran, so that path is unchanged. On the fall-through path the reload put the same byte in A and set N/Z the same way; AND #&C0 then sets A, N and Z from A again, so A, X, Y, N, Z, C, V, D and memory match at the BNE and on every later path (the loop, INY/BNE, move_to_next_column, which loads X and then sets A by TYA). Stack depth is unchanged. The interrupt: irq1_handler does a read-modify-write of ACCCON (AND #&FE, so only bit D changes and the X/Y paging bits stay), puts ROMSEL back from &F4 after sfx_tick, and does not write &CE/&CF or scenery sprite data. So both reads would see the same paging and the same byte even with an interrupt between them, and the MOS path does not write game sprite data either. Cost: LDA (zp),Y is 5 cycles, 6 when it crosses a page, and 2 bytes.

Machine lens holds. Removed LDA (zp),Y is B1 CE: 2 bytes, 5 cycles, +1 when (&CE)+Y crosses a page (read, so the +1 applies); 65SC12-legal, no decimal/RMW issues. AND #&C0 sets N/Z from the same A, so state at BNE is identical. BNE back to find_end_of_column_loop and BEQ to move_to_next_column are short, now 2 bytes nearer: still in range. Scenery sprites are static data in bank 4 sideways RAM (no stores to scenery_sprite_* anywhere in src/); any IRQ paging change that was not restored would already break the first load of the original, so the reload adds no protection. Section is cmos = TRUE. Executions 17.1/5 = 3.42 a pass matches the window's measured cycles.

    AND #&0F
    EOR sfx_p_lo,X

    ADC #&80
    ROL A

Most of the movers that miss fail this test (8.8 of 17.1 a pass), and a mover that fails x <= mover_x_max always passes it. Then test x <= mover_x_max as a branchless 16-bit compare (the way the range prefilter does), exiting straight to the RTS with C=0 instead of through CLC/RTS. The TAY and the reload of movers_x_low go. Also adds a CLC/RTS stub after the always-taken BEQ, so that check_for_mover_collision_with_mover_X's BEQ (taken 5.5 times a pass) no longer crosses from &24xx to &25xx. The friendly count, the common case, is the taken branch (-2). Hits run the same code, moved below the tail. check_if_friendly's C picks the same counter (BCS to INC friendly, else INC unfriendly then BRA). Each path reaches consider_target with the same A, the same C (1 friendly, 0 unfriendly) and N/Z from the INC, which LDY target overwrites. The facing test: after the compares, C=1 means the current target is at or beyond the candidate. LDA #0 / ROR A puts C in bit 7 (C becomes 0), and EOR frame_and_flip flips it when facing left. So N=1 exactly when the old code reached found_target (facing right and C=1, or facing left and C=0), and BPL goes to consider_next_enemy otherwise. A (now the EOR result, not frame_and_flip) and C (0) are dead there: next come DEX/BPL, then CPX #2 or the prefilter's loads, or the collision check, which starts with CPX mover_to_update and never reads A. When X was 0 it now BRAs to search_done, where LDX target loads 0 exactly as the old fall-through did. At search_done, LDX target; BPL check_if_friendly is the old BMI no_target / JMP check_if_friendly with the branch sense inverted. Target 0..11 goes to check_if_friendly with X=target and N=0; that routine reads only X and mover_to_update, sets A, Y and C itself, and its skeleton BEQ arrives with C=1 from the CMP. Target $FF falls to SEC/RTS with X=$FF, N=1, Z=0, C=1 and V untouched, the same exit state as before. Page-crossing and the project's 'no data moves' rule (tables and interrupt variables shift by 2) are for the machine/project lenses.

The flip path itself checks out. BRA (&80) is a real 65SC12 opcode. Taken, it is 3 cycles and stays in its page (&29AC -> &29B3). The old tail BIT abs (4) + BPL not taken (2) = 6 becomes BRA 3, so 3 cycles are saved on the flip path. The code grows by 2 bytes (-2 saved). V differs at the new label, but nothing reads it (sfx_tick has no BVC/BVS, and RTI restores P). The flip_pending => irq_owned invariant also holds: wait_for_timer_281a is reached only after take_irq_for_play, and every way back to give_irq_back goes through render_finish -> render_to_main (wait_for_flip, then STZ flip_pending). The claim fails on what the 2-byte slide does to a hot indexed read. The argument says 'Slid indexed tables all small, far from page ends', and that is wrong. kc_slot0_y (src/kindcache_build.6502:467, SKIP 257, the kind cache's slot 0 offsets) is in the slid region. I rebuilt both in scratch: it moves &3247 -> &3249 in the shipping build (RELEASE 0 and 1) and &324B -> &324D in the -Shift 256 -ShiftEnd build. kc_draw's 'LDY yo,X' and kc_restore's 'LDY ryo,X' (src/kindcache.6502) are self-modified to KC_Y0 - 1 + kc_off. They read each byte of the slot's offsets once a draw and once a restore, X counting down from the row's count. A 12-column helicopter body (up to 257 bytes, at least 186 to reach the page) runs from &3247 past &3300. So the row group that straddles &3300 gets 2 more page-crossing reads (+1 cycle each) in the draw and 2 more in the restore. That is about +4 cycles each pass a slot-0 cached part is drawn and put back. It can be -1/-2 instead if a group's base lands on &32FE/&32FF, depending on the sprite's row counts, so it is not even a fixed sign. Those are the helicopter bodies the cache exists for, drawn every pass they are on screen, so this can cancel or exceed the 3 cycles a pass. The claim did not count it. Also uncounted, in the shipping build only (the -Shift build has neither): BCS set_frame_and_flip_3149 starts crossing (+1 when taken, firing at a target behind), and kindcache_build's BPL unflipped (&30FD -> &30FF, in the waits) stops crossing (-1). Branch ranges are fine (BNE/BPL no_flip offsets &2E->&30 and &29->&2B). The SKIP before &3400 absorbs the 2 bytes (&3348 -> &334A), and the KC_Y0 + KC_CAP0 <= &3400 ASSERT still passes (&334A). So 3 cycles a pass is not the net figure on the measured game, and it is not shown to be no slower.

With a carry it goes to INX, then BCS back (C is still 1, INX leaves C). So A, X, C and V are identical at skip_overflow_307f. Y is untouched (still the collision routine's value, dead, and reloaded at is_on_screen). grep shows no other reference to skip_overflow_307f. The same zero page is read and nothing is stored. At skip_overflow_307f, old and new have the same A, X (vrh+carry, mod 256), C (INX leaves it, so the BCS back is always taken) and V (from the ADC). N/Z differ, but CPX &C5 overwrites them immediately. There is no BVC/BVS in game.6502. Exit: unchanged .next RTS; caller PLAs romsel, restores A/Y/X from the stack, and RTI restores P, so the annotation's live C/V at LDX #3 are not really live. Each non-final iteration's INY moves after the BEQ; INY does not affect AND's Z, and AND sets Z afresh. The extra-byte INY/BNE is unchanged. It exits by BEQ with the same Y (the zero's offset), A=0, Z=1, N=0, and C and V as they came (the old JSR'd routine touched neither). X is untouched.

move_to_next_column (also JMP'd from scroll_hazel's unpack_scenery_column with Y the zero's offset): A = low + Y + 1 mod 256, and X = high + the carry of the 9-bit sum low + Y + 1 (at most 511, so one carry). Y and N/Z come from LDY edge_and_layer on both tails, so the BPL 'always branches' still holds. The column tail costs 27 old against 21 new with no page carry (6 saved), and 28 against 24 with a carry (4 saved). A full walk saves 20 (18 on a carry), and HAZEL's JMP move_to_next_column entry saves 6 (4). That matches the claimed 20. Nothing writes into the region (no self-modifying operands, no label+N entries). The removed labels are referenced only inside the window. set_scenery_sprite_address_from_XY stays. The unpack path: callers 1090/1385 go BPL, DEC, LDY, CPY; the 1201/1297 paths go through consider_* and back to CPY. move_forward_through_sprite is reached only by the JMP at 1489, from calculate_sprite_address_for_column_of_scenery, which is called at 1134 and 1287. The only values ever written to flip_pending are &80 (this store, the only setter) and 0 (STZ in the IRQ, render_reset and render_to_main), so bit 7 clear means it is 0. From then until here nothing sets it, and the IRQ can only STZ it again, and interrupts are off anyway (SEI) from before the field is chosen. So the DEC always takes 0 to &FF. Every reader tests only bit 7: BIT flip_pending / BPL in the IRQ, prebuild and BMI in wait_for_flip; the harnesses (passlock, helilock, scrollleft, worldrun) use & 0x80. BIT also copies bit 6 into V, &FF against &80's 0. In the IRQ, V is not read after the BIT (LDA/STA/AND/ORA/STZ follow, then BIT irq_owned sets V again, and RTI restores the interrupted P). In prebuild, the BIT with the flip pending is followed by SEC/SBC, which sets V before anything could read it; with the flip done the byte is 0 in both versions. wait_for_flip only returns once the byte is 0, so it leaves V=0 in both. On exit: original A=&80, N=1 Z=0; new A = the flip field (A is dead: update_movers' caller does JMP main_game_loop, which starts with LDX/JSR keydown_int, and the observer loop does LDX/JSR check_for_keypress), and N=1 Z=0 from DEC's &FF result, the same flags. It also breaks the rule 'No data moves, no new RAM' and decision 36's documented 231. The fix is the padded variant, or pinning KC_M1 to its old address. Recount: LDX #imm (2 cycles, 2 bytes) plus LDA #imm (2 cycles, 2 bytes) gives 4 cycles and 4 bytes.

The direct saving is right: LDX #&00 and LDA #&00 cost 2+2 = 4 cycles and 4 bytes on the 65SC12, and A and X are dead after both JSR start_column callers. The argument about the slide is wrong, though. It says everything that moves stays 'within pages &2E/&2F' and that 'none of the slid code has an indexed read'. The argument named the variables but not the table. The proposer's scratch assembly must have stopped looking at &2F4C, the end of compiled_back, before INCLUDE kindcache_build. C3, the byte-neutral alternative, avoids all of this.

summary: The long run's end offset goes into the fill loop's CPX as a self-modified immediate (STA abs at line 216) instead of zero page &F8. The fill loop's CPX zp (3 cycles) becomes CPX # (2), saving 1 cycle per byte filled. The store, skipn's LDX and mergen's CPX each use the operand absolute, which costs +1 cycle and +1 byte each. Net about 0.3 cycles a pass, 3 bytes larger.
equivalence: filln, skipn and mergen are local to the unpack_scenery_column scope and referenced nowhere else in src/. All three are reached only through line 216, which now writes the same value (A = X + n) to the CPX's operand that it used to write to &F8. Every later read in the run (the fill's CPX, skipn's LDX, mergen_loop's CPX) reads that operand. So X, A, Y and the flags are the same at every exit (JMP next with the same X and Y): CPX #v and CPX abs set NZC as CPX zp does for the same v, and LDX abs sets flags as LDX zp does. The operand is rewritten before every read, because each long run passes line 216 first. So its initial #0 never matters, and prebuild/pre_undo need not save it: it carries nothing between runs. &F8 (end_of_run_offset / mover_x_low) is now left holding n (line 212's store) instead of X + n. The routine's header and prebuild.6502's measurement both say nothing reads it after the walk before writing it, and prebuild saves and restores it as before. move_to_next_column sets every flag it leaves (ADC, LDY), so no other difference can be seen.
relies_on: HAZEL (&C000-&DFFF, ACCCON Y set through play) is writable RAM, and this code only runs from there: unpack_for_play writes this code into it. &F8's value after the unpack is dead (routine header; prebuild.6502's pre_zp_list measurement). Forward reference to a '= * + 1' label is the same idiom as cm_full_below_operand in game.6502. Page crossings: the change is at the very end of hazel_b (&DDF3 on). filln moves &DE05->&DE06 and its BNE stays on page &DE. mergen_loop's BNE also stays on &DE. No hot code follows: hazel_b_end moves &DE31->&DE34, and ASSERT <= &E000 still holds. The exit flags, Y, &88 and &B6/&B7 are dead or overwritten: add_Y_rows' 10 rows always reach add_delta, and BIT # touches only Z. The proof depends on the firing mover's screen address high byte being in &40-&7F, and that is not guaranteed. The movers_screen_address_low/high tables (game.6502 around lines 836-844) load as all &00, and nothing initialises them, not even start_game. A slot gets a real address only when its mover touches a screen edge (calculate_screen_addresses_for_mover_on_edge, lines 1847/1849). check_if_mover_can_be_updated updates any mover up to viewport_right+&0A, which means it can move and fire there. So a newly spawned mover just past the right edge runs on its stale address. On the first game that address is &0000. move_mover_left then calls subtract_delta_from_screen_address_in_AX, and from &00xx that gives a high byte of &FF: &00-&00 with the borrow is &FF, and CMP #&40 / BCS skips the fix-up, so the address only stays in the ring if it was already >= &40. With X >= &80 the old and new code give different results, because the old add_delta subtracts &40 on every step whose high byte has N set, whether or not there was a carry. Example: &FFF0 with n=7. The old code goes &FF->&BF, &C0->&80, &80->&40 and ends at &4028. The new code carries out of lo+56, INX gives &00, BPL is taken, and it ends at &0028. With no carry at all, the old code reaches &7F after two steps while the new code leaves &FF. The projectile's movers_screen_address_high+12 is game state. The renderer passes it to world_of_address (render.6502 lines 1069-1070 and record_live 2242-2246) to place and draw the projectile, so the state, and possibly the screen, can differ from the original. The path is a never-placed slot firing right just past the right edge (for example at an ally helicopter or the tank) in the first game, which the scripted proofs are unlikely to reach. I could not show that path is unreachable, so by the rule the candidate is refuted. The other claims hold: projectile_x_offset (&88) has no alias and its exit value is dead; add_Y_rows with Y=&0A always rewrites delta_low/high; nothing enters past the label; the line is neither protected nor generated. Recount: each old iteration (LDY #, JSR, add_delta at 42 cycles, DEC zp, BNE) costs 58 cycles, so the old total is 58n+2 (466 at n=8). The new code takes 20 cycles on the BCC path, about 446 saved at n=8, as claimed. Bytes: old 11, new 19, so the code grows by 8.

skeptics.reason: The rewrite matches add_delta(+&0008) only while X < &80 at the loop's entry. Old: X' = X + C, then X' - &40 if bit 7 is set. New: X unchanged when C=0; when C=1, INX and then &40 if bit 7 is set. With X in &80-&FE they give different results (for example X=&FF, C=0: old &BF, new &FF; X=&A0, C=1: old &61, new &40). Nothing in the code guarantees the ring invariant that the argument relies on. X comes from movers_screen_address_high,Y (line 4015), and that table is assembled as all &00 (line 842) and never zeroed or seeded into the ring at game start: only the edge routine (1849), the per-move store (2879) and use_player_position (2912) write it. subtract_delta_from_screen_address_in_AX does not bring a value below &40 back into the ring; it keeps any result >= &40, including &80-&FF. So a slot still holding &0000 that moves left once (&0000 - &0008 = &FFF8) or up (rows_up keeps anything >= &40 the same way) gets a high byte of &FF/&FE/&FD. A mover can be updated, moved, turned and made to fire while up to &0A past viewport_right (check_if_mover_can_be_updated), before its edge sets its address. Enemy helicopters do exactly that: they move vertically, flip direction when no target is found, and then call consider_mover_firing_bullet. The SAM always takes this path. The dataflow annotation agrees: at entry it says X=? and after add_delta X=0..191, so the analysis does not prove X < &80 either. If that happens, the projectile's movers_screen_address_high + 12 differs. The step 2 renderer reads that through world_of_address, record_live and the rec_sh comparison, so the state and possibly the screen differ from the original's. I have not shown in a run that this path is hit, but the precondition is not established and I am not sure it holds, so: refuted. Everything else checks out: the loop count and exit, projectile_x_offset = 0, and Y, delta_low/high (add_Y_rows with 10 rows always crosses a group and rewrites them before any read), C and V (rewritten by that crossing from A and X alone), the stack depth and the interrupt are all fine.

The in-line code itself is right for the 65SC12: CLC/ADC #/BCC/INX/BPL/LDX #/DEC zp/BNE/BEQ are all NMOS opcodes, the new block (&28B7-&28C6 shipping) stays in page &28 so no branch in it crosses, BNE back is -16 and BEQ forward +5, both in range, and X+C <= &80 gives the same &40 wrap as add_delta for any X in &00-&7F. Per iteration, old is LDY# 2 + JSR 6 + add_delta 42 (45 when it wraps; its BPL at &193D does not cross) + DEC 5 + BNE 3 = 58; new is 7 (no carry), 11 (carry) or 12 (wrap) + 8, so it saves 43 (39, 41) an iteration, 344 a call at 8 iterations. The block is 16 bytes against 11, +5, so code and data from &28C2 to &3347 move up 5 (the SKIP to &3400 absorbs it; 184 bytes free). The claim does not count what that move does. 1) kc_slot0_y, slot 0's offsets array in the kind cache (SKIP KC_CAP0 in src/kindcache_build.6502, included at game.6502:5077), moves from &3247 to &324C. kc_draw's LDY yo,X and kc_restore's LDY ryo,X (src/kindcache.6502, operands self-modified by kc_bases to KC_Y0-1+kc_off) read it with X = the row's count, and abs,X reads pay +1 across a page. The &3300 boundary moves from index &BA to &B5 of the array. For any 12-column sprite over 180 bytes cached in slot 0 (&15 has 257, &45 214: the helicopter bodies, which decision 36 cached because they dominate the late frames), drawn and restored on every pass while it is on screen: a row with kc_off < &B5 that reaches past &B4 gains up to 5 crossings; a row with kc_off in &B5-&B9 loses every crossing it had (up to the row's count minus a few). Each of these happens on both the draw and the restore. The net per pass depends on how the rows split (y mod 8), can go either way, and can be larger than the claimed 5.8 cycles a pass. 2) Branches whose page crossing changes after the move (listing addresses): &29EE BCC consider_next_bit_2f3d in multiply_A_by_X_2f1e's 8-step loop starts crossing (+1 per taken bit); &2BC4 BCS set_frame_and_flip_3149 starts crossing; &2E10 BPL update_score_loop, &2FFB BRA count_column, &3011 BCS not_cachable and &30FD BPL unflipped (kind cache build) stop crossing. None of the indexed reads of tables inside the region changes page. The &3000 boundary: only kg_begin's last bytes (&2FFB-&2FFF) cross it, and that code is already continuous with code above &3000, so they are not run with ACCCON X set. The IRQ's flip_* variables (&29D8 on) stay below &3000. So 5.8 cycles a pass (0.017 calls a pass) is not this change's effect on the pass: the render side's change from moving kc_slot0_y is not counted, its sign is unknown, and it lands on code that runs every pass. Refuted until it is measured (passbench with helicopters cached in slot 0), or until the 5 bytes are made up within the block so nothing after it moves.

summary: In pre_cancel, CMP #&80 becomes ASL A. At that point pre_valid is 1, &FF or &80, and ASL gives 0 only for &80. It is a byte shorter at the same 2 cycles. A=&80: CMP gives Z=1 C=1 N=0; ASL gives 0 with Z=1 C=1 N=0, so BEQ done is taken as before and the exit flags are identical; A leaves as 0 instead of &80. A=1: CMP gives C=0 Z=0; ASL gives 2 with C=0 Z=0, so the branch is not taken as before. N differs, but the next LDA rewrites N and Z, and C is the same. A=&FF: CMP gives C=1 Z=0; ASL gives &FE with C=1 Z=0, so the same branch and the same C. On the cancel path A is reloaded at once, and C/V pass through pre_undo (in:CV out:CV) and PLA/STA, so that exit is identical. The only difference anywhere is A = 0 instead of &80 on the &80 path. The routine's contract is 'A, X changed', and both callers write A before reading it. reset_screen_scroll runs STZ pre_valid, STZ last_dir, LDX, STX, LDY, STY, STY, DEX, STX, LDA #&08. start_clear runs STZ, STZ, PLP, JMP initialise_column_buffer, which loads X and stores with STZ; start_column's contract leaves A = 0. Neither instruction touches V, and Y is untouched. Nothing refers to pre_cancel + n (grepped). ROMSEL and its copy are untouched on the &80 path either way.

Of every branch from &DB87 to hazel_b_end (&DE31), only edge_right's iteration-8 BNE * + 7 changes. It goes from crossing (at &DBF9: next &DBFB, target &DC00) to not crossing (at &DBF8: next &DBFA, target &DBFF). I checked this by script over build/strykers.lst and by assembling in scratch; no branch starts crossing. The only indexed absolute read of data that moves, LDA squares,X (&DD12, X 0..3), stays in page &DD. Executions: edge_right's LDA edge_x_low costs 1005 cycles in 1500 passes on seed 1 and 834 in 600 holding RIGHT (build/grind/pc-*.json), which is 0.22 and 0.46 calls a pass. The BNE is taken unless mover 8's x low byte equals the edge's, so about 0.34 a pass averaged. hazel_b gains a byte of room. pre_cancel's &80 path ran in 2 of 30 calls in 1500 passes on seed 1; the common 0 path (24 of 30) is untouched.

N differs (bit 7 of A-&80 vs bit 6 of A) only on the fall-through, where LDA os_ram_copy rewrites N and Z at once; on the &80 exit both leave N=0. A leaves 0 instead of &80 on that exit only. Only two entries (JSR pre_cancel at &1E94 reset_screen_scroll and &2EF4 start_clear; no pre_cancel+N references in src/ or tools/), and both write A before reading it: reset_screen_scroll STZ/STZ/LDX/STX/LDY/STY/STY/DEX/STX/LDA #&08; start_clear STZ/STZ/PLP/JMP initialise_column_buffer (LDX #20, STZ loop, LDA #0). No memory, ROMSEL, stack or Y difference; the interrupt saves and restores A. Same cycles in pre_cancel (2 vs 2). The opcode is fine: ASL A (&0A) is a real 65SC12 opcode, 2 cycles like CMP #imm, and Baron takes 'ASL A' (bank5.6502 uses it). The pre_cancel paths keep their cycles. In edge_right, iteration 8's BNE moves from &DBF9 to &DBF8 and its target from &DC00 to &DBFF, so it stops crossing a page: 1 cycle saved when taken. But the claim that 'the only indexed absolute read of data that moves is LDA squares,X' is wrong. src/kindcache.6502:45 sets KC_M1 = hazel_b_end, so slot 1's masks array starts at hazel_b_end. Removing the byte moves it from &DE31 to &DE30, and KC_CAP1 = (&E000 - KC_M1) DIV 2 grows from 231 (&E7) to 232. KC_P1 stays at &DF18. The renderer reads those masks with kc_draw's self-modified AND &FFFF,X (.mo, src/kindcache.6502:235). Its base is kc_mbl/kc_mbh + kc_off = KC_M1 - 1 + kc_off, and X counts from cnt down to 1. With the masks one byte lower, each row's base sits one byte lower against the &DF00 boundary. For example, a row at kc_off = &CF has base &DF00 now and no crossings; after the change its base is &DEFF and every one of its cnt reads takes the +1. A row one byte earlier loses one crossing. So the masks' per-read cycles change, in either direction depending on which cached kind's rows land there, and the claim neither counted nor measured this. The capacity check in kindcache_build.6502:166 also now accepts a 232-byte kind into slot 1, which changes which kinds the cache can hold. That is data moving (the grind's 'no data moves' rule) and a change in behaviour that the argument does not consider. The 1-cycle BNE saving is real, but the net count is unknown, so it is refuted.

The kind cache builder runs kg_begin and kg_start on every build start, which happens whenever a new kind is wanted, almost certainly far more often than once every 1000 passes.
